sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (central-level unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate or tax registry distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic codified system under the 1991 Constitution; commercial and corporate matters codified in the Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, and Ley 1258 de 2008 for the S.A.S.)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (approved by Law 1143 of 2007; in force 15 May 2012)
UK-Colombia-Ecuador-Peru Trade Agreement (continuity free trade agreement; in force 1 January 2021)
Colombia-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2010; in force 2013)
Colombia-Spain Double Taxation Agreement (approved by Law 1330 of 2009)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Alianza del Pacifico; signed 2012, in force 20 July 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), articles 98-116, 137-158 and 980; Ley 2155 de 2021, article 63, and DIAN Resolución 000164 de 2022 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF); Ley 526 de 1999, article 6, and Decreto 1068 de 2015, Libro 13 (UIAF and AML/CFT framework); Superintendencia de Sociedades External Circular 100-000005 de 2021 (SAGRILAFT for the non-financial supervised sector); Código Penal (Ley 599 de 2000), articles 323 and 326 (money laundering and financing of terrorism offenses); Código de Procedimiento Administrativo (Ley 1437 de 2011).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RUBF filings are made to the DIAN and accessible exclusively to DIAN, UIAF and competent supervisory authorities; the beneficial-owner registry is not public)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., UK Companies House; U.S. Secretary of State; equivalent authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Colombia acceded on 27 June 2000; Convention in force from 30 August 2000); consular legalization if the issuing state is not a party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by foreign shareholders to Colombian legal counsel or representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention; consular legalization for non-party states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of corporate resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the S.A.S. and subscription of quotas
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretariat or board of directors of the parent entity, notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention; consular legalization for non-party states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors and legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of each person's citizenship, with notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention for foreign notarized copies; domestic Colombian notarization where the person is present in Colombia

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Executed by each UBO before a Colombian Notaría
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization in Colombia (no apostille required); for foreign execution, notarization plus Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; (iv) Colombian UIAF consolidated warnings lists and the national PEP roster maintained by Función Pública; and (v) available Interpol notices and adverse global media. Screening must be performed pre-incorporation, on any change of control or beneficial ownership, and at minimum annually; all positive and negative screening records must be preserved for ten years under Código de Comercio article 28 and applicable AML/CFT guidance. A negative-match certification signed by the legal representative must be retained before filing the RUBF and opening any commercial bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (https://www.rues.org.co), administered by Confecámaras; the name pre-consultation certificate (certificado de homonimia) is issued by the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate documents and bylaws must be drafted in Spanish. Foreign-language instruments, including parent resolutions and powers of attorney, must be apostilled (or consular legalized) and translated into Spanish by an officially certified translator (traductor oficial) registered with the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores before filing with the registry. Corporate names must use Latin-script Spanish orthography; no transliteration into non-Latin scripts is permitted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bancario, Financiera (prior authorization of Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia required)
Cooperativa (Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria clearance required)
Universidad, Colegio, Escuela, Liceo (Ministerio de Educación Nacional authorization required)
IPS, Clínica, Hospital, Salud (Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social authorization required)
Radio, Televisión, Telecomunicaciones, Emisora (Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones authorization required)
Petróleos, Minera, Carbón, Hidrocarburos (Ministerio de Minas y Energía authorization required)
Nacional, Presidencial, República (official or state connotation requiring approval of the Ministerio del Interior or other competent authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No formal extension of the 30-day name reservation is available; a new pre-consultation must be requested after expiry. Upon rejection: (i) file a new RUES pre-consultation within five business days using a differentiated name token (e.g., prefix/suffix such as Global, Group, Sys, Consulting, or a distinct spelling variant); (ii) if the rejection asserts identity or confusing similarity with a registered name, file a written reconsideration petition (derecho de petición, Ley 1755 de 2015) with the issuing Cámara de Comercio; (iii) if the Chamber upholds the refusal, file the administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within ten business days of notification under Ley 1437 de 2011, articles 74-76; and (iv) simultaneously reserve an alternative name to protect the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a registered service address physically located in the municipality designated in the bylaws; the address must be able to receive judicial notices, DIAN correspondence and Cámara de Comercio communications. Coworking and virtual-office addresses are accepted by Colombian Chambers of Commerce for low-risk, license-exempt SaaS entities provided the operator commits to receiving service of process. A PO Box or purely electronic address is not a valid statutory domicile. Books and records must remain available at the registered office or another disclosed Colombian location; remote teleworking of employees does not by itself create a permanent establishment risk if management decisions are taken in Colombia.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months and 10% over a three-year horizon for a license-exempt, low AML-risk helpdesk SaaS. DIAN may verify the registered address, invoicing, and RUBF compliance, and the Cámara de Comercio may conduct domicile verification at registration; any mismatch between the registered address and the actual location of records or personnel materially increases inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and homonymy certificate (solicitud de certificado de homonimia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or competent local Chamber)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff under Decreto 1074 de 2015; approximately COP 48,000 (USD 12 at 4,000 COP/USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel fee for drafting the S.A.S. bylaws (estatutos) and incorporation filing pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Bogotá market benchmark for a standard S.A.S. pre-incorporation pack (USD 450-800)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), codified under Código de Comercio arts. 98–109 (complementary), Ley 222 de 1995 art. 22, and Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015 Title III; registration governed by art. 6 Ley 1258 and Cámara de Comercio regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) – no public deed required unless real property is contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital (Ley 1258 art. 4); capital may be zero or nominal, subscription and deferred payment permitted up to 2 years; no escrow account required for this non-regulated service entity; capital must be deposited in a bank account and certified upon payment
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST SHAREHOLDERS' MEETING OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. The undersigned shareholders resolve: (1) to approve the subscription of shares and initial paid-up capital in accordance with the bylaws; (2) to adopt the bylaws and corporate purpose for software helpdesk and customer support services; (3) to establish the registered office at [address], Bogotá D.C.; (4) to appoint [NAME] as Legal Representative and [NAME] as alternate; (5) to authorize opening bank accounts, executing contracts, and completing RUES and DIAN registrations; (6) to appoint a statutory auditor if required. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name pre-validation and availability certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio through RUES online portal (https://www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to 3 proposed corporate names through the online pre-approval module 'Consulta de Homogeneidad de Nombres'. Provide the intended activity codes (ISIC 6201) and shareholder identification data. Receive the Certificado de Homogeneidad de Nombres valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Identification documents (cédula or passport) of all subscribing shareholders
Proposed corporate names list
Enumeration of the corporate purpose with ISIC code 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected for similarity, immediately re-file with alternative names via the same online module; no fee is charged for re-validation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the private incorporation document and bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (optional for private document execution) / direct execution by shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución conforming to Ley 1258 de 2008, including bylaws, shareholder registry, capital distribution, term (indefinite), and representation clauses. Execute the document before a notary if any shareholder is absent or for authenticity enhancement; otherwise, execute privately. Stamp tax (impuesto de timbre) applies where applicable.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation document and full bylaws
Copy of the valid name availability certificate
Identification document of each subscribing shareholder
Proof of capital payment (if partially paid) or payment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify, rectify the affected clauses (SUIN legalization or capital contribution issue) and re-present; notarial refusal does not invalidate a private document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (online filing via jurisdictional portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed incorporation document and supporting dossiers to the Chamber's digital registration system. Pay the registration fee (derechos de inscripción), registry tax (impuesto de registro), and processing fee via PSE bank transfer. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio and assigns the NIT (Tax ID).
required_dossiers: Executed Documento Privado de Constitución
Name availability certificate
Payment receipts for registration tariffs
Shareholders' identification and RUT (if pre-registered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'nota devolutiva' (return note), correct all observations within 30 days and resubmit electronically; lodging a formal reconsideration request is available under Código de Procedimiento Administrativo (Ley 1437 de 2011).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: DIAN tax registration (RUT) and tax classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – online module 'Registro Único Tributario'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Chamber registration is completed, the RUT (NIT) is auto-activated; access the DIAN portal to confirm the tax classification: Régimen Ordinario (not SIMPLE due to annual revenues), responsible for ICA and VAT, and register as a software/helpdesk service exporter if applicable (for VAT 0% exportation benefit under Decreto 2094 de 2015).
required_dossiers: Chamber of Commerce registration certificate
NIT auto-assigned number
Legal representative identification and digital signature
Lease contract or office proof for the fiscal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT activation, correct the KPI/KPO data (address, responsible regimes) and re-submit; request a 'cita virtual' (virtual appointment) at the DIAN contact center to resolve discrepancies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Compensación Familiar (e.g., Colsubsidio), ARL (e.g., Seguros Bolívar), EPS and Pension Fund Administrators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and its first employees in the integral social security system via the official 'Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes (PILA)' platform. Enroll the company with an ARL for occupational risks (risk class based on CIIU 6201 – low risk), an EPS for health, and a pension fund (AFP).
required_dossiers: Company NIT and RUT
Lease contract or registered office proof
Identification documents of employees
PILA enrollment form and initial payroll declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PILA returns an inconsistency, correct the employee data and re-submit within the same fortnight; late filings attract fines, so submit a corrective planilla immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account and commercial operations launch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current account (cuenta corriente or cuenta de ahorros) presenting the Chamber of Commerce certificate (less than 90 days old), NIT/RUT, and identification of the legal representative. Secure the digital token for banking transactions and activate Stripe Billing / PayPal integration in the company name.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio (issued within last 90 days)
RUT/NIT
Legal representative identification and passports (if foreign)
Resolution of appointment of legal representative
Proof of registered office (utility bill or lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to PEP status or document issues, provide a legalization letter from a Colombian attorney or choose an alternative bank; a formal complaint can be filed with the Superintendencia Financiera if discriminatory denial occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) – Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos under Ley 1581 de 2012 (mandatory personal-data processing registry) and Alcaldía Municipal (local pre-industrial license for office premises)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos Personales (mandatory for helpdesk/SaaS data processing) – no industrial manufacturing permit required; if physical offices are opened, a Certificado de Uso del Suelo (land-use compatibility certificate) and Sayco-Acinpro public performance license (if music is played) are required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national projects; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) for Bogotá D.C. and municipal environmental authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – CIIU 6201 (software helpdesk and support services) is classified as a low-environmental-impact service activity under Decreto 1076 de 2015, so no EIA study, environmental permit, or registration is required; only standard municipal waste-disposal compliance applies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015 (pH 6.0–9.0, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L for non-discharging offices connecting to municipal sewer); no VOC emissions are generated from software operations – internal air quality governed by Resolución 2254 de 2017; e-waste (computers and hardware) must be channeled through a qualified post-consumer program under Resolución 1512 de 2010

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Cumplimiento de Seguridad Humana y contra Incendios (yearly fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos) mandatory for any physical office with more than 10 workers; compliance with the Sistema de Gestión de la Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) under Decreto 1072 de 2015 and Ley 1562 de 2012, including the Plan de Emergencias and structural load inspection for multi-story occupancy; labor office (Ministerio del Trabajo) inspection can be triggered by workplace accidents or employee complaints – mitigation requires completing periodic ARL medical examinations, updating workplace risk assessments, and maintaining the Registro de Afiliación to ARL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: www.dian.gov.co, MUISCA electronic platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a SAS must first register the company with the Cámara de Comercio through the RUES system; DIAN then issues the NIT automatically upon company registration. The company must update the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) online, obtain an electronic signature certificate, and activate the NIT for electronic invoicing. Non-resident foreign suppliers of digital services without a local entity must register for a foreign-entity NIT through DIAN’s special procedure and may appoint a tax representative where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Colombian SAS is taxed as a corporation at entity level, not as a pass-through, and territorial income principles apply for the corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Colombian law. An SAS may elect the SIMPLE combined regime if eligible (gross income below 80,000 UVT), and certain new small enterprises may elect the ZESE or other temporary tax incentive regimes, but no hybrid-mismatch or pass-through classification election is available for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - Value Added Tax, supplemented by consumption taxes and municipal fees where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold triggers compulsory VAT registration; registration is required from the first peso of taxable supply or import. Foreign digital service suppliers supplying services to non-business consumers in Colombia must register for VAT and each invoice/import operation, regardless of turnover. The optional SIMPLE regime, available to small taxpayers with gross annual income up to 80,000 UVT, is not an exemption from VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all VAT-responsible entities and must be issued through DIAN-authorised software generated under the factura electrónica de venta with real-time prior validation. Invoices are transmitted via API/web services to DIAN’s MUISCA platform; each invoice receives a unique electronic identification code (CUFE or CUDS) and digital stamp before delivery to the customer. Continuous electronic audit file submission is required, and deviations are subject to administrative sanctions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating is available only when the goods are physically exported from Colombia to a destination outside Colombian customs territory and the export is evidenced by a valid DEX customs declaration. For services, including helpdesk, conversational bot and cloud support services, zero-rating applies when the service is rendered to and 'used or enjoyed' abroad by a non-resident customer, provided the service falls under Article 481 of the Colombian Tax Statute and meets the material export-verification rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX electronic export declaration accepted by DIAN with exit confirmation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Certificate of inward foreign exchange repatriation or Exterior Remittance Certificate
Contract or service agreement demonstrating the offshore recipient and offshore use for services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts transfer-pricing and export-fraud audits with a five-year statute of limitations; incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT clawback, default interest, and severe administrative penalties, including inaccurate-invoice penalties of up to 100% of the omitted VAT. Documentary falsity or intentional abuse may constitute tax fraud and smuggling-related offences carrying criminal penalties and possible disqualification from tax benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through the Junta Directiva and the Comité de Reglamentos de Cambio, with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia authorized to supervise regulated foreign exchange intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a partially regulated capital account. Current account transactions, including service exports from helpdesk and software activity, are generally freely convertible through the foreign exchange market on the basis of bank-supported declarations. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment into a CO_SAS, profit remittances, loan principal repayments, and outbound investment, must be registered with Banco de la República to acquire legal repatriation rights. For an ISIC 6201 helpdesk subsidiary, profit remittance is permitted after payment of Colombian corporate income tax and the applicable dividend withholding tax on non-resident shareholders, provided the original equity injection was registered and the remitted amount is supported by audited financial statements and documentary evidence of goodwill, invoicing, and operational substance in Colombia.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds derived from software, helpdesk, support, and cloud services rendered by the Colombian S.A.S. must be channeled exclusively through an authorized intermediary of the Colombian foreign exchange market (a supervised commercial bank). The statutory channeling obligation must be completed within the regulatory timeline set by Banco de la República, commonly no longer than six months from the date of service billing or receipt, with authorized extensions available in justified events. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% for foreign currency proceeds from service exports, unless the bank has formally enabled a permitted foreign currency deposit account and the bank registers the exemption; no partial voluntary conversion ratio applies. The channeling requirement is enforced through the submission of the corresponding foreign exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) to the receiving bank, with the service invoice, signed contract, and proof of actual delivery of support services kept in the AML/KYC dossier.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in COP and USD with foreign exchange intermediary registration capabilities
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account for foreign investment registration
Operational Account in COP; selective USD account support for non-resident-owned S.A.S.
Operational Account and foreign exchange declaration channel

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI accounts, such as Wise Pro, Payoneer, Payoneer B2B, or Deel-type payment partners, have no standing to execute the mandatory Colombian foreign exchange declaration or to register foreign investment with Banco de la República. They may serve only as auxiliary settlement rails for small-value inbound subscriptions or platform payouts where no Colombian legal FX obligation arises, but they cannot replace a licensed Colombian intermediary for dividend repatriation, export proceeds channeling, foreign capital entry, or tax remittance. Use of an offshore EMI as the principal treasury account creates a high compliance risk for the CO_SAS and may lead to unregistered capital flows and administrative sanctions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally available for a low-risk helpdesk S.A.S. when the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner hold valid identification and submit notarized or apostilled corporate documents. However, Tier-1 banks in Colombia commonly require at least one physical or videoconference-assisted interview of the legal representative or of a specifically empowered local corporate officer for foreign-controlled S.A.S. entities. For USD accounts and for foreign investment registration reporting, the bank's compliance unit normally insists on a physical presence visit at the Bogotá or Medellín corporate banking center, or a formal local power of attorney accompanied by direct verification calls to the foreign director. The anticipated legal result is that director travel and branch appearance will be necessary for the first corporate account opening event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual or corporate ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain above the CO_SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structure chart from the ultimate human beneficiary to the Colombian entity; apostilled and notarized incorporation documents; certified copy of the S.A.S. bylaws and shareholder registry; current UBO and legal representative identification; source-of-wealth memos for each injection; three months' corporate bank statements of the ultimate parent; audited financial statements, if any; professional reference letter from the home-country bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cloud helpdesk and customer support revenues settled through Stripe, PayPal, or similar PSP into a foreign account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed customer agreements reflecting true helpdesk and software services; itemized support tickets and SLA delivery evidence; platform payout statements; intercompany master and local transfer pricing documentation; Colombian foreign exchange declarations for every material collection; proof of payroll and social-security filings for Colombian support engineers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound subscriptions or professional fees from affiliates classified as concealed dividends or intercompany payments without economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transfer pricing contemporaneous report under Peruvian? Under OECD-aligned Colombian TP rules; functional analysis evidencing the Colombian entity's administrative, operational, and financial risk; description of software platform infrastructure owned locally; board minutes approving the commercial policy; banking records showing collection-disbursement segregation; local VAT/ICA/tax clearance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Minimum capital contribution and no physical Colombian office triggering 'shell company' red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for Colombian premises, utility bills, payroll evidence, employment contracts, helpdesk telephony and ticketing records, local compliance policies, Colombian tax registration, and a detailed business plan substantiating ongoing operational activity. For bank onboarding, an evaluation of the S.A.S. as a going concern with sustainable cash flow may be requested.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders must remit capital to the Colombian S.A.S. via SWIFT MT103 directly to the conventional account opened with a Tier-1 Colombian bank, using a mandatory reference to 'foreign investment' and the corporate tax ID (NIT). The receiving bank will direct the transaction to the proper foreign exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional) contained in the Colombian FX regime; the funds must be registered with Banco de la República through the bank's online system before being released for operating purposes. All supporting evidence, including the signed capital contribution minutes, apostilled shareholder resolutions, source-bank records, and the investor's identification documents, must be uploaded to the compliance queue. Proceeds cannot be routed through a private individual's account, a non-bank PSP, or an offshore EMI; such routing invalidates the investment registration and blocks future dividend repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for international software vendors, cloud infrastructure, subcontractors, and shareholder distributions must be executed with SWIFT MT103 payment instructions from the Colombian screen-based bank platform, using correct FX purpose codes and the underlying invoice or board resolution. For larger capex or one-off procurement with counterparties requiring payment guarantees, a commercial letter of credit is permissible under UCP600 and is normally issued by the Colombian bank's trade finance desk. Local COP-denominated operating disbursements to Colombian vendors, employees, and tax authorities may use ACH/PSE-type domestic clearing rails. Cross-border disbursements are always subject to the Colombian FX declaration framework; the treasury file must preserve the invoice, terms of trade, invoice attestation by the foreign counterparty, and the bank confirmation for each rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/COP deliverable forward contracts with a Colombian authorized commercial bank for documentary trade receivables and payables
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP settled with established broker-dealers for non-resident-entity-only hedging
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for intercompany long-term debt or capital hedging purposes
USD/COP FX options through regulated Colombian financial institutions when executed for hedge-treasury purposes and evidenced under IFRS hedge accounting
Central-bank-approved FX swap transactions for managing short-term liquidity mismatches

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registration Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of each calendar year (mandatory annual renewal window January 1 - March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers monetary fines under Código de Comercio and, if the registration is not renewed for 6 consecutive months after the deadline, the Cámara de Comercio may declare caducidad (administrative expiration/strike-off) of the mercantile registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Estados Financieros de Asamblea Aprobados (Annual Financial Statements Approved by Shareholders and Filed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (filing after shareholder approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval by March 31; filing with Cámara de Comercio within 1 month of approval (statutory cut-off for most S.A.S.: April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve or file may expose the company to Superintendencia de Sociedades administrative sanctions and, where books/registered statements are not filed, to the standard Chamber proceeding against the registrant; persistent non-compliance may lead to loss of good standing and potential forced strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual tax calendar issued by DIAN; normally based on the last digit of the NIT and falling in September/October each year for prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of the tax payable for each month of delay (up to 100%), plus monthly default interest; failure to file also enables DIAN to carry out an official assessment, and persistent non-compliance can lead to inactivation of the NIT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Información Exógena / Beneficiario Final (Annual Exogenous Fiscal Report Including UBO Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing calendar published by DIAN; generally due during August (windows vary by NIT) for reported information from the prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or inaccuracies may trigger DIAN penalties of up to 5% of the value of omitted transactions or up to 260,000 UVT in formal fines, plus receipt of reminder/filing requirements; non-filing does not itself cause strike-off but impairs fiscal compliance and increases tax enforcement risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit (Revisor Fiscal) is compulsory for a Colombian S.A.S. when, as of the preceding December 31, total assets or gross annual revenue equal or exceed 5,000 monthly legal minimum wages (SMMLV), or when the company has more than 50 employees, is listed, or engages in certain supervised activities; the helpdesk SaaS entity normally becomes audit-mandated only if these quantitative or qualitative thresholds are met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes) as adopted in Colombia by Decreto 2420 de 2015 and subsequent amendments; full NIIF (IFRS) is required where legal/fiscal thresholds for large entity classification are exceeded.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation with the Cámara de Comercio. Instead, the S.A.S. must disclose its final beneficial owners (beneficiario final) annually in the Información Exógena submitted to DIAN, and any intermediate share transfer must be documented in the share transfer records and entered in the shareholder book. Direct changes in ownership or control are also reportable to the Cámara de Comercio in the event of a legal reorganization, membership change or increase of capital.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Colombia applies a single headline CIT rate of 35% for taxable years beginning 2024 and 2025. Preferential income tax treatment is available only in narrowly defined circumstances: Free Trade Zone (FTZ) entities enjoy a reduced 20% rate on income derived from the FTZ; certain research, development, and technological innovation investments may generate a 25% or 30% income tax discount under Article 256 of the Tax Code; and software producers may access accelerated depreciation and VAT exemption on qualifying exports, but no general low-tax ICT patent box or notional IP deduction is available. Colombian holding companies electing the CHC (Compañía Holding Colombiana) regime may benefit from reduced taxation on dividends and capital gains from foreign subsidiaries, subject to economic substance conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed through DIAN's MUISCA electronic portal (http://www.dian.gov.co) with mandatory prior electronic signature and NIT (Numero de Identificación Tributaria) registration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline falls in the period from the 9th to the 21st calendar day of April following the fiscal year-end (fiscal year must be 31 December for a standard S.A.S.), the exact date being assigned by DIAN based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. Extensions are not granted beyond this DIAN calendar; quarterly prepayments (pagos trimestrales) are compulsory during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification header: NIT, tax return year, economic activity code (ISIC / CIIU 6201), and whether the filing is original or amendment (corrección).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident nominal shareholder of an S.A.S. does not file Form 110 in Colombia; the S.A.S. itself files and reports the non-resident's NIT or passport identification in the shareholder schedule if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenues generated by the helpdesk, customer support and conversational bot cloud operations, including recurring SaaS fees, usage-based metering, implementation fees, and related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue subject to Colombian source rules must be reported; if the non-resident's services are performed outside Colombia and no Colombian source is present, only revenues attributable to a Colombian permanent establishment or Colombian exploitation are included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary costs and deductible operating expenses, including cloud hosting, subcontract labor, telecommunications, software amortization, personnel, and headcount costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs paid to non-resident related parties must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and invoicing (factura electrónica) to be deductible; payments to jurisdictions with preferential regimes are elliptical and may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (renta líquida gravable) after offsetting prior-year tax losses, exempt income, and other special deductions permitted by the E.T. (Estatuto Tributario).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot report Colombian taxable income on behalf of the S.A.S.; the S.A.S. is the taxable entity. If a CFC or PE scenario exists from the non-resident side, home-country reporting is separate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 35% on the net taxable income, before applying tax credits, withholding tax certificates, and treaty credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No withholding tax credits of the non-resident can be used in the S.A.S.'s return; the S.A.S. computes its own Colombian tax after considering foreign tax credits on foreign-source income, if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax loss carryforward offset claimed in the current year, subject to the 12-year rule and to the availability of the fiscal loss certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is a corporate attribute; it remains with the entity even when shares are transferred to a non-resident. Change of control may trigger anti-abuse review, but does not automatically forfeit the loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income tax and complementary tax due, minus advance payments and withheld taxes, producing either a balance payable or a saldo a favor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A saldo a favor can be claimed by the S.A.S. by way of electronic compensatory filings; non-resident shareholders cannot offset such balance against Colombian dividend withholding taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 110 incurs a monthly penalty equal to 5% of the tax payable, capped at 100% of the tax, or 1% of gross income per month if no tax is due, capped at 100% of gross income; minimum penalty is 18 UVT (approximately COP 1,117,530 for 2025). Late payment of income tax attracts interest (intereses moratorios) computed daily at the DIAN rate plus a 10% fine on the unpaid tax amount. Submission of inaccurate returns may trigger the 'sanción por inexactitud' of up to 200% of the understated tax, and non-filing can result in asset seizure and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia applies a final withholding tax of 10% on dividends distributed to non-resident beneficial owners to the extent the distributions are paid out of profits that were already subject to corporate income tax at 35%. Where the DTA (e.g., the Colombia-Spain, Colombia-Chile, or Colombia-Korea treaties) is applicable, the dividend withholding rate may be reduced to 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 20% of the capital directly for a 12-month holding period, or to 10% or 15% in other cases. To invoke treaty relief, the recipient must (i) be the beneficial owner; (ii) obtain a Colombian Fiscal Residence Certificate (Comprobante de Residencia Fiscal, CRF) from its home tax authority; (iii) submit the CRF and a Form 110-related annex to the withholding agent at or before the payment date; and (iv) register the beneficial owner in DIAN's electronic withholding system. For refund of over-withheld dividend tax, the non-resident must file a special refund claim (Form 100 / Solicitud de Devolución) through MUISCA, attaching the CRF and evidence of withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties for software IP, patents, know-how, and licensing: 15% when the beneficial owner is a non-resident without a Colombian permanent establishment; statutory withholding on interest paid to non-resident lenders: 15%, reduced to 10% for loans from foreign financial institutions or certain development banks; where a DTA applies (for example, Colombia-Spain protocol), royalties may be reduced to 7.5% or 10% and interest to 10% or 12%, depending on the treaty and the character of the payment. Technical service fees that are effectively a royalty are recharacterized and subject to the same 15% withholding. All payments to non-residents require the payer to obtain a CRF and submit a Colombian withholding certificate (Certificado de Retención) to both the DIAN and the payee.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The mandatory Local File and Master File obligations apply to an S.A.S. with total gross assets or gross revenues exceeding 100,000 UVT (COP 4,847,192,000 for 2025) or to taxpayers whose foreign-related-party transactions exceed 10,000 UVT (COP 484,719,200 for 2025). Additionally, a formal Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 120) must be filed annually when the taxpayer reaches the 100,000 UVT threshold or carries out cross-border transactions with related parties above the de minimis amount, even if the annual return shows no tax. The S.A.S. helpdesk company must also provide a contemporaneous TP study for any cross-border intercompany cloud hosting, software royalties, management service fees, or technical support charges.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime for ordinary commercial companies; however, economic substance is consequential for (i) claiming benefits under tax treaties, (ii) qualifying as a Colombian Holding Company (CHC), and (iii) rebutting the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR / abuso en materia tributaria) contained in Article 869 of the Tax Code. A shell S.A.S. without real staff, premises, activity, or decision-making in Colombia will not be recognized for treaty or CHC purposes. In the software context, DIAN may scrutinize the true situs of server operations, support functions, client contracts, and intellectual property ownership to prevent conduit arrangements. Transfer pricing penalties of up to 200% of the understated tax and the automatic disallowance of the payment are triggered when substance and documentation fail to demonstrate arm's length behavior.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: International Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Underreporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial reduction of Colombian-source revenues from the helpdesk SaaS contracts, such as invoicing through an offshore shell without real substance, underreporting recurring subscription income, or registering clients in a low-tax jurisdiction without migration of actual support personnel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Colombian tax criminal law (Código Penal Tributario, Law 1943/2018 as complemented by Law 2277/2022), tax evasion exceeding 250 monthly minimum wages (approximately COP 325,000,000 for 2025) is punishable by imprisonment of 48 to 108 months and fines up to 15,000 SMMLV; false or inflated cost invoices generate a penalty of up to 200% of the understated tax, plus cancellation of the RUT (tax registration) and criminal referral. DIAN may impose daily administrative fines of up to 10,000 UVT and secure the disqualification of the taxpayer from public procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and administrators of the S.A.S. who intentionally conceal revenues or who approve the use of simulated contracts are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall and related penalties under Article 794 of the Tax Code and Article 78 of Law 1258/2008. Criminal judges may impose travel bans, asset embargoes, and confiscation of luxury property; upon a final criminal conviction, the director faces imprisonment for up to 9 years and civil restitution of at least 300% of the evaded sum.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Substance Sham
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a domestic Colombian S.A.S. as a mere letterbox to route support fees to an offshore sister entity, or maintaining nominal local employees and no actual management authority in Colombia while the board and commercial decision-making are entirely conducted abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the shell under the economic substance doctrine and reattribute the revenue to the Colombian entity, imposing a 35% tax plus a penalty of 200% of the underpaid tax and a monthly late-payment interest surcharge. For violations of the SAS law, the Superintendencia de Sociedades may dissolve the company and order the liquidation of assets for sham transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 42 of Law 1258/2008, shareholders and directors who use the S.A.S. as an instrument of fraud, tax evasion, or abuse of corporate assets are personally liable. The civil court can pierce the corporate veil and order the director to pay all debts of the entity, including withholding taxes and social security obligations. The legal representative may also be barred from leaving Colombia while criminal and tax investigations are pending, and in aggravated cases, the director is sentenced to 6 to 12 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the S.A.S. in the Colombian Commercial Registry (Cámara de Comercio), or accepting payments through unregulated crypto/money transfer channels inconsistent with the declared Stripe or PayPal rails, without implementing 'Know Your Business' controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering aggravating penalties under Law 1762/2015 authorize imprisonment of 10 to 30 years if illicit proceeds are disguised through corporate vehicles. The S.A.S. can be fined up to 1,000 SMMLV (approximately COP 1.3 billion) for failing to maintain UBO records; and the commercial registration can be cancelled, leading to involuntary dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal responsibility for approving transactions that involve unverified third-party funds. Under Colombian anti-money laundering jurisprudence, a director who knowingly signs off on suspicious client onboarding or uses PayPal/Stripe as straw intermediaries can be indicted for 'lavado de activos,' resulting in preventive imprisonment, a ban on managing commercial companies, and the seizure of all personal and corporate assets linked to the alleged illicit activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Cross-Border Cost Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Colombian helpdesk S.A.S. excessive management fees, support fees, or cloud licensing fees from a foreign parent or sister company without applying the arm's length standard and without preparing a contemporaneous TP study or filing Form 120.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN will adjust the taxable income and disallow the overstated deductions, applying a 35% additional CIT plus a penalty of 200% of the understated tax on the adjustment. Failure to file Form 120 triggers a fine of 5% of the aggregate value of the related-party transactions or up to 10,000 UVT, and the TP documentation itself, if false, can generate a 'sanción por inexactitud' of up to 100% of the tax determined by DIAN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The administrator who signs the Form 110 swear that the expenses are true and arm's length becomes personally liable for the assessed tax adjustment if the supporting evidence is proven fictitious. Severe cases may be prosecuted as aggravated fraud, carrying imprisonment of 6 to 9 years, a ban on holding public office, and an order to pay restitution of the full tax debt plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Remit Withholding and VAT on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Netting or delaying the withholding tax (15% or 10%) owed on royalties, technical assistance fees, or dividends to non-residents, or failing to accrue and remit VAT (IVA) on the import of digital services from abroad at the new 19% rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agents who fail to declare and pay at source are liable for a fine of up to 200% of the amount not withheld or paid and daily late interest; DIAN may automatically reject the deduction of the underlying payment. The S.A.S. can also be held jointly liable for the foreign beneficiary's Colombian tax deficiency when the payment was made without proper withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally decide to omit withholding liabilities are subject to personal joint liability for unpaid taxes and penalties. If the amount exceeds 4,000 UVT (approximately COP 193,887,680 for 2025), the director may face criminal tax evasion prosecution, leading to imprisonment of 3 to 7 years, civil restitution, and a travel ban pending payment of the full tax damage.
